claims.text: Merges to Anthropic's monorepo went from about 2,500 a day in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September, most of them by Claude.
claims.quote: Merges to its monorepo went from about 2,500 a day in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September.

claims.text: Anthropic has about 25 million CI checkouts a day, which fetched naively would be over 600 PB of Git traffic a day.
claims.quote: there are about 25 million CI checkouts a day

claims.text: Anthropic's post says Git's offline, full-clone design was actively undermining its ability to scale, because nearly all its clients are now always-online agents and jobs.
claims.quote: was actively undermining our ability to scale as the repo grew

claims.text: Scion inverts Git: the server keeps history and does blame, commits, merges and rebases, refs move by a compare-and-swap on one row, and clients fetch only the trees and blobs they need.
claims.quote: The server keeps history and does blame, commits, merges and rebases; refs move by a compare-and-swap on one database row

claims.text: Because Scion's objects are immutable, three tiers of cache each serve more than 99% of reads.
claims.quote: Objects are immutable, so three tiers of cache each serve more than 99% of reads.

value.unit: percent of reads served by each cache tier

claims.text: By Anthropic's figures Scion uses about 200 times less CPU and memory than the Git mirrors it replaced, and the migration took five months and seven engineers.
claims.quote: about 200 times less CPU and memory than the Git mirrors it replaced

value.unit: times less CPU and memory than the Git mirrors

claims.text: Anthropic says Scion is by no means a suitable replacement for git for general use.
claims.quote: by no means a suitable replacement for git for general use

claims.text: sgit started from the same instruction Anthropic arrived at: Git solved most of the hard problems, so copy Git, with encryption underneath and a dumb server.
claims.quote: Git solved most of the hard problems, so copy Git.

claims.text: In the words of the March brief, sgit's server is a dumb key-value blob store and all intelligence lives in the client.
claims.quote: a dumb key-value blob store

claims.text: sgit's clone and pull walk fetches only what is needed, level by level over the trees, then the blobs in batches of 50 with 16 requests in flight.
claims.quote: level by level over the trees, then the blobs in batches of 50 with 16 requests in flight.

claims.text: Every sgit object is named by the SHA-256 of its ciphertext and checked against its name, and the name says whether it is immutable, so anything between storage and reader can keep it for ever.
claims.quote: Every sgit object is named by the SHA-256 of its ciphertext, and the client checks each one against its name.

claims.text: sgit.ai's documentation pages, a vault read in the browser, load 18 objects cold, then one 69-byte ref, then nothing inside a two-minute window.
claims.quote: 18 objects cold, then one 69-byte ref, then nothing inside a two-minute window.

value.unit: objects fetched on a cold load

claims.text: The server sends a one-year immutable cache header, but the CDN in front of the hosted API does not yet serve object reads from its cache; browsers, clients and static hosts do.
claims.quote: the CDN in front of the hosted API does not yet serve object reads from its cache; browsers, clients and static hosts do.

claims.text: Neither Scion nor sgit packs objects on the server, and both treat having no packfiles and no maintenance as a feature.
claims.quote: Neither system packs objects on the server, and both treat that as a feature.

claims.text: Scion protects directories with permissions on a server that holds plaintext; sgit protects them with keys, one vault per trust domain, so the server has nothing to protect and can be anyone's.
claims.quote: Scion protects directories with permissions on a server that holds plaintext. sgit protects them with keys

claims.text: On 16 October the vault the newsroom's agents share had 1,295 commits, 5,281 files and about 35,000 encrypted objects, 527 MB with all its history.
claims.quote: On 16 October it had 1,295 commits, 5,281 files and about 35,000 encrypted objects, 527 MB with all its history

value.unit: encrypted objects in the newsroom's shared vault

claims.text: A full clone of the shared vault is the worst case: three and a half minutes for 35,423 objects, but no agent takes one.
claims.quote: A full clone is the worst case: three and a half minutes for 35,423 objects.

claims.text: One 130-file folder with one commit of history clones in 13 seconds and 3 MB, 137 objects, however large the vault is.
claims.quote: one 130-file folder with one commit is 13 seconds and 3 MB, 137 objects, however large the vault is.

value.unit: seconds for a one-folder, one-commit clone

claims.text: An 83-file vault took 59 seconds to clone with sgit 0.22.0 because two batches exceeded the Lambda's size limit; the development branch splits a refused batch and takes about 11 seconds.
claims.quote: an 83-file vault took 59 seconds to clone with sgit 0.22.0, because two batches of objects were over the size limit of the Lambda

value.unit: seconds to clone an 83-file vault with sgit 0.22.0

claims.text: The time is the distance to the storage, not sgit: the same one-folder clone takes 0.8 seconds against a local API server, and the small vault cloned in 1.6 seconds from a plain file server.
claims.quote: And the time is the distance to the storage, not sgit.

claims.text: Against a local API server the one-folder clone takes 0.8 seconds and the full clone 69.
claims.quote: the one-folder clone takes 0.8 seconds against a local API server, the full clone 69.

value.unit: seconds for a one-folder clone from a local server

claims.text: sgit has path history, signed authorship, signed tags and verification, but no blame and no bisect, because its server cannot read a commit.
claims.quote: Today sgit has path history, signed authorship, signed tags and verification, but no blame and no bisect.

claims.text: A partial clone of a long history still walks the commits one request at a time, so a folder with all 1,295 commits takes nearly four minutes unless a depth is given.
claims.quote: a partial clone of a long history still walks the commits one request at a time, so a folder with all 1,295 commits takes nearly four minutes, and a depth avoids it

claims.text: Git and sgit live side by side rather than in sync: there is no bridge that turns Git history into sgit history or back.
claims.quote: there is no bridge that turns Git history into sgit history or back.

claims.text: Agents change what source control is for: the clients are always online, the volume is machine-scale, and the expensive thing is moving bytes nobody needs.
claims.quote: Agents change what source control is for: the clients are always online, the volume is machine-scale, and the expensive thing is moving bytes nobody needs.

claims.text: The two designs meet in the middle on immutable objects, fetching only what is needed, no packfiles and compare-and-swap.
claims.quote: The two designs meet in the middle on immutable objects, fetching only what is needed, no packfiles and compare-and-swap.

claims.text: Scion could not keep a merge queue at its rate, so concurrent changes can conflict and Claude typically fixes them; the merge went back to the agent, which is where sgit keeps it.
claims.quote: concurrent changes can conflict, but Claude can typically fix these conflicts

claims.text: The practical difference is availability: Scion is a blog post, and sgit is pip install sgit-ai today, with its code in the open.
claims.quote: sgit is pip install sgit-ai today, with its code in the open

claims.text: The useful next steps are on the client: a small encrypted record of the commit chain, blame as a fold over path history, and testing at a much larger scale.
claims.quote: a small encrypted record of the commit chain so a partial clone does not walk history, blame as a fold over path history, and testing at a much larger scale.

claims.text: sgit is not proven at Scion's scale; its largest vault in daily use is about 35,000 objects and ten agents.
claims.quote: sgit is not proven at Scion's scale. Its largest vault in daily use is about 35,000 objects and ten agents.

claims.text: The measurements are one run each, from cloud sandboxes; a plain connection does better.
claims.quote: The measurements are one run each, from cloud sandboxes. A plain connection does better.

claims.text: The fix for the small vault's slow clone is not released yet; it is on the CLI's development branch.
claims.quote: The fix for the small vault is not released yet. It is on the CLI's development branch.

claims.text: Scion's figures are Anthropic's, from its post, and not independently verified.
claims.quote: Scion's figures are Anthropic's. From its post; not independently verified.

claims.text: The owner has a stake: sgit is ours.
claims.quote: I have a stake. sgit is ours.
